The file `capi-shell-plugin-api-endpoint-proxy-provider-capo.sh` is a bash function that queries a Kubernetes cluster for an OpenStack cluster's API endpoint using `kubectl` and `yq`. The function accepts namespace and name parameters, constructs a `kubectl` command to retrieve an `openstackcluster` custom resource, parses the YAML output with `yq` to extract the control plane endpoint, and echoes it. There are no suspicious network requests, no obfuscated code, no use of `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, or `wget`, no exfiltration of local data, and no unexpected system modifications. The operations are entirely contained within standard Kubernetes tooling and serve the application's stated purpose.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for capi-shell:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This bash script is the main `capi-shell` application that sets up a shell with CAPI cluster kubeconfig and provider environment variables. Analysis reveals no evidence of malicious code injection. The script uses standard packaging and application patterns: it reads a YAML config via yq, sources plugin .sh files from `/usr/share/capi-shell/plugins/`, fetches a base64-encoded kubeconfig secret from Kubernetes, transforms it with yq, and launches a shell. The `source "$_plugin"` loop is a documented plugin mechanism — any code in those plugin files runs with user privileges, which is expected application behavior, not a supply-chain attack. The `envsubst` call substitutes env vars in config values, which is standard. No curl/wget/eval/base64-assembled payloads, no exfiltration, no reverse shells, and no execution of remote code.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>No malicious behavior detected; standard CAPI shell application code.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard BATS (Bash Automated Testing System) unit test file for the `capi-shell-plugin-capo` package. It tests an API endpoint proxy that interacts with Kubernetes/OpenStack clusters via `kubectl` and optionally establishes SSH tunnels via `sshuttle`.

The file creates stub binaries for `kubectl` and `sshuttle` to simulate various cluster configurations and tests that the proxy correctly extracts host/port information, handles cleanup of background processes, and skips when no provider reports an endpoint. All commands (`kill`, `bash -c`, `source`) are standard testing patterns within the BATS framework. There are no network requests to untrusted hosts, no data exfiltration, no obfuscated code, and no suspicious file operations. The XML escape sequences (`'`, `"`, `<`, `>`, `&`) are artifacts of the file's XML representation, not obfuscation.
</details>
<evidence>

LLM auditresponse for multi-capi-shell:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a legitimate bash helper script (`multi-capi-shell`) that enables interactive selection of CAPI (Cluster API) clusters and launching of `capi-shell` sessions for them. The script reads configuration from environment variables and a user-owned config file at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/capi-shell/config.yaml`, uses standard tools expected for a Kubernetes cluster management tool (`kubectl`, `yq`, `fzf`, `capi-shell`), and supports both interactive (`fzf`-based) and direct (`--direct`) modes.

No genuinely malicious behavior was found. There are no network downloads of executable code (no `curl|bash`, `wget`, etc.), no obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads, no `eval` of untrusted input, no data exfiltration, no backdoor mechanisms, and no tampering with unrelated system files. The `envsubst` call on line reading the config file's kubeconfig paths is a legitimate feature allowing variable expansion in the user's own config file, not a supply-chain attack vector.

The `fzf` preview command uses `awk` only to display formatted text (context@config), not to execute commands. The `yq` expressions properly use `--arg` for safe variable passing. All operations are consistent with the stated purpose of interactively managing CAPI clusters.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Legitimate CAPI cluster management helper script with no malicious behavior.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
